title: Modular Branching and the Good-Node Crystal

items.title: The cogood node gives the simple socle and head of the residue induction
items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$, $\mu$ a $p$-restricted partition
of $d$ and $i\in\mathbb Z/p$ with $\varphi_i(\mu)>0$; let $B$ be the cogood
$i$-node and $\nu=\mu\cup B$
([[def-residue-signature-normal-good-conormal-and-cogood-nodes]]). Then
$F_iD(\mu)$ has simple socle and simple head, both isomorphic to $D(\nu)$,
and the total (ungraded) multiplicity of $D(\nu)$ in $F_iD(\mu)$ is
$\varphi_i(\mu)$
([[def-generalized-jm-primary-idempotents-and-residue-summand-functors]]).
items.strategy: Construct the endpoints locally from the accepted essential root-interval basis: last-column upper-unipotent factorization forces every first-level primitive deficit terminal and each line one-dimensional; hats characterize normality. Integral choose-two tensor operators compute a central transposition-sum scalar, and compensated splitting plus the zero criterion prove exactly the good cyclic modules simple. All Schur socle labels are restricted, so an explicit no-killed-submodule and Se-tensor corner-lifting argument identifies the group socle, including columns and degree one via an unused coordinate. Centre differences locate residues; nondegenerate quotient forms give the restriction head. Prove correct finite-coset Frobenius and projected Hom adjunction, apply the true labelled good/cogood inverse to identify the unique induction socle, and use the self-adjoint primary projection on the induced coset form for its head. Total multiplicity is a separate PENDING use of the corrected conormal-count supplier at bottommost conormal B; no whole-target READY until that supplier has a complete accepted local proof. Delete the false unused epsilon_i(mu+B)=phi_i(mu) premise. The endpoint proofs and all-field/empty-partition cases do not depend on the count.
